subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should macOS Dashboard browser injection be limited to configured shared token/password auth, or may it reuse native/stored device tokens for GUI/native parity?
rationale: The current PR fixes the linked security-boundary report, but the sibling Dashboard auth issue and PR intentionally preserve native-token parity, so automation cannot choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Adopt shared-token-only browser injection
options.body: Rebase this PR, update show, showConfiguredWindowIfPossible, and handleEndpointState to use the shared-token-only helper, require macOS proof, and close or supersede the native-token parity sibling.

options.title: Keep native-token parity
options.body: Close or pause this PR and continue with the sibling Dashboard auth parity PR after proving native-token browser injection is intended and safe.

options.title: Design an upgrade-safe transition
options.body: Preserve existing fallback behavior until maintainers define a documented migration or explicit strict boundary that avoids surprise Dashboard auth failures.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared-token-only browser injection
recommendation.body: Rebase this PR, update show, showConfiguredWindowIfPossible, and handleEndpointState to use the shared-token-only helper, require macOS proof, and close or supersede the native-token parity sibling.
